blocks.text: Truth tables show the truth values of logical statements. A truth table lists every possible combination of the input truth values and shows the result for each combination (Fig 2.5). Truth tables are important in propositional logic, are widely used in computer science and mathematics, and help check that logical expressions are correct.

blocks.caption: Figure 2.5 Truth table for AND, OR and NOT

blocks.text: The main purpose of a truth table is to show how a logical expression behaves: when it is true and when it is false. Because it lists all possible inputs, it removes confusion, lets us check complex expressions easily and compare different statements, and helps in decision making.

items: Identify the propositions (for example A and B).
List every combination of True and False for them.
Apply the connectives step by step, one column at a time.
Write the final result for each row.

blocks.text: Each proposition such as P or Q can take the value True (T) or False (F). A truth table lists all possible combinations, which is 2^n rows for n propositions: 4 rows for two propositions and 8 rows for three. The truth value of a compound proposition is decided by the values of its parts.
